name: The Best Rolled Sugar Cookies
headnote: Submitter J Saunders presents this as the only rolled sugar cookie recipe she uses, and warns that anyone who tastes them will ask for a copy. She adds that she ices them with a confectioners' sugar and milk mixture thinned just enough to brush on with a pastry brush without running off the cookie. Allrecipes' editors (contributions by Vanessa Greaves) append a long technique section: cream the butter and sugar four to five minutes until pale and airy, keep the butter cool but pliable, whisk the dry ingredients separately, mix only until no dry streaks remain, and chill at least an hour so the cookies hold their shape. They also stress measuring flour by fluffing and spooning rather than packing, rolling to an even thickness, using parchment, spacing cutouts an inch apart, and loading only a fully cooled sheet.
comment_digest: The most-voted review (7,789 helpful, Shannon Dailey) calls the dough reliable for cutouts but adds an extra cup of sugar and a teaspoon of vanilla, plus 1/4 to 1/2 cup more flour in humid climates, and dusts with powdered sugar rather than flour when it turns sticky. That extra sugar and vanilla is the most repeated fix; reviewers with 1,930 and 1,266 helpful votes also chill overnight, keep most of the dough refrigerated while working a quarter at a time, and freeze the cut shapes briefly so they hold their edges. One with 823 votes instead dropped an egg and a cup of flour for a more buttery cookie. Almond extract and citrus zest are common additions. Bake time is the usual mistake: it suits roughly 2-inch cutters, so larger ones need 12 to 13 minutes and thin ones only 8 to 9. Dissenters report dough too soft to roll even after overnight chilling.
flags: Headnote is a mix of the submitter's short note and a long Allrecipes editorial section; both paraphrased. Several reviews are truncated with 'Read More' in the paste, so only visible text was used.
